cases.name: a-listed-column-drawn-without-replacement
cases.description: distinct="true" on a repeating text column. Without it the same tag can land twice in one cell, which is normal and often wanted; with it the row's values are drawn from the pool without replacement.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="6" seed="d1" local="en"><sequence name="T"><gen type="text" value="news,tech,sport,food,travel" repeat="3" separator=", " distinct="true"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{T}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: the-same-column-on-the-in-memory-engine
cases.description: The engines are not merely both correct, they agree value for value: distinct draws off a #dist sub-stream keyed the same way in both, so the cells are identical to the case above.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="6" seed="d1" local="en" mode="memory"><sequence name="T"><gen type="text" value="news,tech,sport,food,travel" repeat="3" separator=", " distinct="true"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{T}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-full-width-list-is-a-permutation
cases.description: Asking for as many values as the pool holds must yield every one of them, in some order. Anything else would mean the draw is not really without replacement.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="4" seed="d1" local="en"><sequence name="T"><gen type="text" value="news,tech,sport,food,travel" repeat="5" separator=", " distinct="true"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{T}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-drawn-generator-has-no-pool-so-it-redraws
cases.description: A number is not a list to draw down. distinct there is bounded rejection sampling on #e{k}r{n} sub-streams — four different values out of five, every row.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="6" seed="d1" local="en"><sequence name="N"><gen type="number" value="1..5" repeat="4" separator=", " distinct="true"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{N}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: the-case-that-asked-for-the-feature
cases.description: A double first name from a WEIGHTED pack. Jesus Jesus Gonzales is not a name. The weights survive — frequent names are still likelier — but the whole-run quota does not, which is why percent= is refused beside distinct=.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="5" seed="d1" local="en"><sequence name="P"><gen type="template" value="person.male.firstName" repeat="2" separator=" " distinct="true"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{P}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: the-anomaly-flag-follows-the-value-that-survived
cases.description: Under distinct the value that survived may have come off a REDRAWN sub-stream. The flag list is resolved on that same sub-stream, so `true` sits beside the element that actually spiked. Resolving it on the first attempt would describe a value that was thrown away — which is what this case exists to catch.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="6" seed="fl" local="en"><sequence name="N"><gen type="number" value="1..5" repeat="4" separator="," distinct="true" anomaly="0.5" anomaly_factor="100" anomaly_flag="F"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{N}} -> ${{F}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: repeat-on-a-drawn-column-under-the-streaming-engine
cases.description: `repeat=` on a generator that DRAWS rather than one that reads a list, resolved one row at a time. A listed column lays every element out at once; a drawn one takes a sub-stream per element instead, and that second road had never been travelled by a test in any implementation — the length plan, the per-element keying and the join all live on it.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="5" seed="unit-test" local="en" mode="disk"><sequence name="R"><gen type="number" value="1..99" repeat="3"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{R}}</data></line></block></tdc>
